impl-rules-check.desc: Three rules that keep impls small and co-located with their types.

rules.rule: Every impl (inherent, or a trait impl for one of our own types such as `impl Default for Foo`) whose self type is a `pub` crate type must live in the same module (file) as that type's definition. Private types are exempt (their impls may live anywhere). `ext_traits` modules are exempt entirely.

Nothing inside a `t` module may call a crate free function, i.e. any call whose path is rooted at `crate::` (or a bare call to a function imported from a `crate::` path). Calls rooted at `self::` or `super::` (which stay within the local type cluster), bare same-file calls, and calls into external crates are allowed. Associated functions are NOT exempt: `SomeType::new()` reached via a `crate::` import is a violation. Enum-variant and tuple-struct construction (`Outcome::Failed(x)`) is not flagged, since the final segment is a type, not a function.
A trait impl for a foreign type (`impl SomeTrait for Vec<T>`, where the self type is not defined in our crate) must live in an `ext_traits` module.

impl-rules-check.rationale: Keep impls scoped to easy helper functions. Preference is free functions over OOP, so an impl method should not reach out into crate logic, and `t` modules should stay self-contained.
